chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Prayer when it is time and the food has been placed. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is at the beginning of the time, begin with the food; and if some of the time has passed, and you fear that it will be lost so you would have to repeat the Prayer, then begin with the Prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the priority between prayer and eating when both are needed at the same time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a dynamic legal principle where the priority shifts based on the urgency of preserving the prayer's validity within its prescribed time window. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing *tahdhir* (preparation) with *hifz* (preservation) of the obligatory act, ensuring that worldly needs do not compromise the spiritual obligation when time becomes critical.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Prayer which had presented itself and the meal is placed. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was at the beginning of the time, begin with the food; and if something from the time had passed, and you fear it would be lost, so you would have to repeat the Prayer, so begin with the Prayer’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Salat (prayer) for which the time has begun and food is made available. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is the beginning of the time for Salat (prayer), then first begin with food; but if the time has passed and you are afraid of missing Salat (prayer) for which you then must do Qada’ (the compensatory Salat), then begin with Salat (prayer) first.’”
